input.question: Broad topic: history of India. Please recommend a comprehensive book that covers it from ancient times to 20th century.
input.ground_truth: Hate to harp on what you've already acknowledged, but South Asia is a very large, culturally/linguistically diverse area that is one of the earliest sites of civilization. Any one book you read is going to leave out a whole lot. It might be better to pick a particular region or time period or cultural phenomena/group that interests you, and then look for a book from there. That said, these are the three that I would recommend: 1) Early India, from Origins to AD 1300 (Romila Thapar) 2) India Before Europe (Catherine Asher & Cynthia Talbot) 3) A Concise History of Modern India (Metcalfe & Metcalfe)

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you want to learn about a big, big story—like the story of a giant tree that has grown for thousands of years. That’s like the history of India!

A good book to learn this story from the very, very beginning (when people first came to India) all the way to the 1900s is called **"India: A History" by John Keay**.

But if you want a book that’s even easier to read and has lots of pictures, you might like **"The History of India for Kids" by Sujata Prasad**. This book tells the story of India in simple words and fun pictures, from the time of kings and queens to the time when India became its own country.

So, if you want the big, big story, "India: A History" by John Keay is a grown-up book that tells everything. If you want a fun, easy story, try "The History of India for Kids" by Sujata Prasad!
